title: Improving time use measurement with personal big data collection - the experience of the European Big Data Hackathon 2019
benchmark_measurement: Not applicable. The paper does not describe a benchmark for language models but rather a data collection system and a hackathon for time-use surveys. No measurements related to faith or religion were performed.
findings: This paper has no relation to religion or faith. The study focuses on a system called i-Log for collecting personal big data from smartphones to improve time-use surveys. It details a pilot study conducted during the European Big Data Hackathon 2019. The activities, data, and analysis discussed are purely secular, focusing on sociological and urban studies, mobility, and daily routines like work, sleep, and travel, with no mention of religious practices, groups, or beliefs.
